Export for a store (presets) What you're doing: producing the edition of your EPUB that a particular store most likes to receive. The book inside is the same; the packaging details differ. Steps Open the Export dialog and choose a preset: Generic EPUB , Amazon KDP , Apple Books , Kobo , Nook , or Draft2Digital . Read the preset's detail panel — it says exactly what changes for that store, in plain words. Download. The filename carries the preset ( your-book-kdp.epub , your-book-apple-books.epub …) so a folder of exports never confuses you. Run the validator on the preset you picked — it checks the package you actually ship, not a generic one. What actually differs KDP & Nook add a legacy guide (cover / contents / start pointers) that older navigation relies on. Apple Books adds Apple's display-options file and rich accessibility metadata. Kobo adds accessibility metadata in the form Kobo's ingestion expects. Draft2Digital combines the lot, since it forwards your book to many stores at once. Identifiers stay honest: if your book has an ISBN, every preset uses it. If it doesn't, presets use the book's own identifier — Beuk never invents an ASIN or a store ID for you. What can go wrong I uploaded the KDP file to Apple. Nothing breaks dramatically — but you'd be carrying another store's packaging. The filename suffix exists precisely to prevent this; trust it. The store still rejected my file. Copy the exact message into the error decoder . Most rejections decode to something small and fixable.
